input: Need to check whether the basement freezer—remind Kira to return the extension cord Sunday.
expected_behavior: Recover an incomplete thought involving the basement freezer, and a separate reminder to remind Kira to return the extension cord Sunday. Do not invent what needs checking about the freezer.
notes: Passes cleanly on checkpoint-520 (epoch 40); failed on checkpoint-26 (epoch 2), which invented "is working" to complete the freezer thought and wrongly promoted it to action_items.

input: Figure out why the tablet keeps—put the donation box by the front door—back to the tablet, the screen goes black whenever the charger moves.
expected_behavior: Recover two intentions: investigate the tablet because the screen goes black when the charger moves, and put the donation box by the front door. The opening and resumed tablet fragments belong to the same intention.
notes: checkpoint-520 correctly reconnects the two tablet fragments but adds a spurious third action item ("Back to the tablet") -- Excessive Fragmentation. Tracked as a known limitation, not yet a clean pass.

input: Ask Celia whether the replacement cable arrived before driving to the office, not ask Celia and separately check the cable, that is one question. The break-room clock is slow again.
expected_behavior: Recover one combined task: ask Celia whether the replacement cable arrived before driving to the office. Recover one separate observation: the break-room clock is slow again.
primary_checks: no unsupported action involving the clock
notes: action_items stays correctly unsplit on checkpoint-520, but the clock observation drops from bullets entirely and a redundant duplicate bullet appears. Tracked as a known limitation.

input: Avery said Morgan moved the boxes to storage. Morgan has the inventory sheet. Ask Avery whether Morgan counted the damaged ones.
expected_behavior: Preserve: Avery made the statement, Morgan moved the boxes, Morgan has the inventory sheet, the writer should ask Avery whether Morgan counted the damaged boxes. Do not claim whether the boxes were counted.
notes: Passes cleanly on checkpoint-520 across all three output fields. checkpoint-26 (epoch 2) misattributed the ask-target to Morgan instead of Avery in narrative and actions.

input: Nina said Cole left the charger with Priya, and Cole said Nina already backed up the photos. Send Priya the folder link. Did Nina back up every photo or only the edited ones?
expected_behavior: Preserve all speaker/actor/recipient roles correctly. Action item: send Priya the folder link. Open question: whether Nina backed up all photos or only edited photos.
notes: Passes on checkpoint-520 (one cosmetic typo, "backped up"). checkpoint-26 severely failed this probe: reversed speaker/actor roles, invented a completed action, and omitted the ###ACTIONS### marker entirely.

input: Tessa told Rowan the permit was approved after she asked about it. She still needs the stamped copy, but I cannot tell whether “she” means Tessa or the inspector. Ask Rowan who needs it.
expected_behavior: Preserve the ambiguity concerning who needs the stamped copy. May resolve the earlier "she asked" to Tessa via ordinary nearest-antecedent reading, but must not confidently assign the stamped-copy need to Tessa or the inspector. Action item: ask Rowan who needs the stamped copy.
notes: Passes cleanly on checkpoint-520, preserving ambiguity consistently across all fields. checkpoint-26 preserved it in narrative but invented an assignment to Rowan -- a third party who isn't even one of the two candidates -- in bullets.

input: Did the refund actually reach the card? Save the confirmation page before closing the browser.
expected_behavior: Preserve an unresolved question about whether the refund reached the card, and a task to save the confirmation page before closing the browser. Do not state that the refund succeeded or failed.
notes: Passes cleanly on checkpoint-520. checkpoint-26 preserved the question but reframed the pending save task as already completed ("I saved...").

input: Was the wet spot from the window or the plant? It was dry again by lunchtime. Put the recycling outside tonight.
expected_behavior: Preserve the unresolved source of the wet spot, the observation that it was dry by lunchtime, and the recycling task. The drying observation does not answer the source question.
notes: checkpoint-520 no longer invents a confident answer (checkpoint-26 asserted the spot "was the plant"), but the question's actual content (window vs. plant) comes through confusingly worded. Tracked as a known limitation.

input: Did I send the revised schedule to Imani or only save the draft, check sent mail—also need to think about the volunteer list, not sure what yet.
expected_behavior: Preserve the unresolved question about whether the schedule was sent to Imani, the task to check sent mail, and the incomplete thought involving the volunteer list. Do not invent a volunteer-list task.
primary_checks: checking task remains connected to the question
notes: Passes on checkpoint-520. checkpoint-26 severely failed: confidently asserted the schedule "was sent" and omitted the ###ACTIONS### marker entirely.

input: The rehearsal felt smoother and the shorter transitions probably helped, print the shipping label, but the final scene still dragged.
expected_behavior: Preserve the rehearsal observations and recover "print the shipping label" as the task.
notes: Passes cleanly on checkpoint-520, task present in all three fields. checkpoint-26 had the task correct in bullets/actions but dropped from narrative, plus a duplicated clause.

input: Pay the registration fee, registration fee by Thursday, the garage light is flickering again and I am tired of dealing with it, do not forget the fee, text Jonah that I will call tomorrow.
expected_behavior: Return exactly two action items: pay the registration fee by Thursday, and text Jonah that the writer will call tomorrow. Do not create multiple registration-fee tasks. Do not invent an action to repair the garage light.
notes: Clean pass on both checkpoint-26 and checkpoint-520 -- the most reliable probe in the suite so far.

input: The walkthrough ran late and the settings explanation was confusing, maybe the screenshots need captions, did Luca ever give Erin the account list, schedule the oil change, the room was too warm, account question still unresolved, and last thing replace the smoke-detector battery.
expected_behavior: Preserve all six topics (walkthrough, screenshot-caption idea, Luca/Erin account-list question, oil-change task, room-temperature observation, smoke-detector-battery task). Action items: schedule the oil change, replace the smoke-detector battery.
notes: action_items is correct on checkpoint-520 (both tasks present), and the tentative "maybe" framing is preserved (an improvement over checkpoint-26), but the oil-change task still drops from narrative. Tracked as a known limitation.

input: Pick up cat food after work. Email the signed form to the school.
expected_behavior: Recover two separate tasks without merging them.

input: The bedroom fan makes a clicking sound at the lowest setting.
expected_behavior: Preserve the observation. Do not invent an instruction to repair, replace, inspect, or contact someone.
notes: checkpoint-520 correctly leaves action_items empty (one harmless hallucinated bullet, "Morning fan"). checkpoint-26 omitted the ###ACTIONS### marker entirely, so this behavior couldn't even be confirmed there.

input: Maybe build a simpler welcome screen with one large button.
expected_behavior: Preserve this as a tentative idea. Do not convert it into a committed action item.
notes: Confirmed regression on BOTH checkpoints against established gold_v1.2 policy (task_plus_idea/observation_plus_idea: ideas belong in bullets, never action_items). checkpoint-520 improved narrative-level hedging ("might"/"considering") and still invents an unrelated fabricated detail, but action_items still wrongly contains the idea as a committed task on both checkpoints.

input: Remember to ask them about the other one.
expected_behavior: Preserve the reminder and its unresolved references. Do not invent who "them" refers to, what "the other one" is, or what answer is expected.
notes: checkpoint-520 correctly avoids inventing the referent (one harmless hallucinated bullet, "Reply to this question"). checkpoint-26 severely failed: invented "my colleagues" as who "them" refers to, and omitted the ###ACTIONS### marker entirely.
